sources.title: Effect of water activity on the crispiness of a biscuit (Crackerbread): Mechanical and acoustic evaluation
sources.authors: J.M. Arimi, E. Duggan, M. O’Sullivan, J.G. Lyng, E.D. O’Riordan
sources.version_or_release: Version of record; Food Research International 43(6), 1650–1655 (2010); DOI 10.1016/j.foodres.2010.05.004
sources.locator: Institutional record abstract; publisher abstract search result; methods section 'Equilibration of Crackerbread to different aw levels' was visible only in indexed result excerpt. Direct repository show-full request timed out at 2026-10-10T06:28:34Z; publisher open returned HTTP 403 at 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Retrieved and read institutional repository record and publisher search result; confirmed citation, methods summary, and article abstract. Full article was not retrieved.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Crackerbread samples equilibrated across aw 0.113–0.98; 5 mm cylindrical probe with Instron; force and acoustic signals captured together. Reported critical aw interval 0.51–0.59 for that product and method. Indexed methods say saturated-salt desiccators at 25 C until constant weight (about two weeks). No general snack threshold is stated.
sources.applicability: Supports pairing a moisture/activity measure with a product-specific fracture/acoustic measure and demonstrates that a threshold is product- and method-specific. Do not transfer its aw interval to the cooperative snack.

sources.title: Sensory texture of commercial biscuits as a function of water activity
sources.authors: G. Hough, M. Del Pilar Buera, J. Chirife, O. Moro
sources.locator: University of Buenos Aires institutional article record, abstract and citation, lines 23–48; opened 2026-10-10T06:28:34Z.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read institutional repository record; full article not supplied by repository.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Four commercial biscuit types were assessed using trained and consumer sensory panels at different water activities. Crispness transition was gradual; perceived loss differed for molar crispness versus sound; ideal aw differed by biscuit type.
sources.applicability: Supports defining the attribute and customer-relevant texture endpoint before setting a pilot rule. Four commercial biscuits are comparators only; no acceptance threshold transfers to the unknown product.

sources.title: Effect of morphology on water sorption in cellular solid foods. Part II: Sorption in cereal crackers
sources.authors: D.C. Esveld, R.G.M. van der Sman, M.M. Witek, C.W. Windt, H. van As, J.P.M. van Duynhoven, M.B.J. Meinders
sources.locator: Publisher abstract and methods excerpt (cracker composition, proofing time); retrieved in search result 2026-10-10T06:29:50Z. Direct ScienceDirect page open returned HTTP 403 at 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Retrieved publisher search result with primary article abstract and indexed method details; did not retrieve full text.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Primary study compared crackers with fine/coarse morphology and used SPI-NMR moisture profiles. The article reports morphology-dependent vapor conductivity and sorption kinetics, including about threefold faster local sorption in the fine-structure cracker at low aw. Its own authors caution against generalizing complex structure-dependent transport without product-specific characterization.
sources.applicability: Supports recording geometry and considering product-specific starting moisture gradients and kinetics. Specific morphology, recipe, and rates are not transferable.

sources.title: Selecting packaging material for dry food products by trade-off of sustainability and performance: a case study on cookies and milk powder
sources.version_or_release: Published article, Packaging Technology and Science 34(5), 303–318 (2021); DOI 10.1002/pts.2561
sources.locator: Ghent University Academic Bibliography abstract, lines 14–27 and citation/version record lines 54–57; opened 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z. Record lists full-text download, but downloaded/read version not used.
sources.observed_operation: Opened institutional bibliographic record and read abstract; direct download link was not followed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Caramelized cookies were flow-packed in PP (reported WVTR 5 g/m2/day), acryl-coated PVdC/PP (4.2), or metallized PP (0.4); stored 22 C/50% RH; the first two lost textural acceptability by six months while MPP extended it. Abstract does not report the WVTR test condition, full pouch dimensions, seal details, or exact acceptance method. A second powder comparison showed humidity-related barrier differences but is not a cookie result.
sources.applicability: Shows comparable constructions and real storage condition, and that barrier choice can alter performance in a specific cookie. Do not compare its WVTR numbers to a supplier datasheet without matched test conditions or transfer its six-month outcome.

sources.title: Chemical and physical changes during storage of differently packed biscuits formulated with sunflower oil
sources.authors: F. Balestra, V. Verardo, S. Tappi, M.F. Caboni, M. Dalla Rosa, S. Romani
sources.version_or_release: Version of record published 2019-07-05; Journal of Food Science and Technology 56, 4714–4721; DOI 10.1007/s13197-019-03918-z
sources.locator: PMC full-text indexed article result, Materials and methods (formulation, packaging materials, experimental conditions, analytical determinations) and abstract; retrieved 2026-10-10T06:30:46Z. Publisher version-of-record page opened 2026-10-10T06:28:34Z; direct PMC open returned recaptcha at 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Retrieved full primary-article content in PMC indexed result and read publisher version-of-record abstract and metadata; the direct PMC page open was blocked by recaptcha.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Same production batch was randomly divided among three materials. Control was metalized OPP/paper; variants replaced the OPP layer with PLA or added EVA to OPP. Bags averaged 300 g filled product and 1,078 cm2 surface area. Accelerated storage was 35 C/50% RH for 105 days; samples were taken at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 85, 105 days. Abstract reports packaging material did not significantly change texture despite differences in moisture, aw, and oxidation indicators.
sources.applicability: Demonstrates controlled batch splitting, construction disclosure, and the need to measure texture separately from moisture. Formulation, accelerated conditions, materials, and duration differ from this case.

sources.title: Delayed Quality Deterioration of Low-Moisture Cereal-Based Snack by Storing in an Active Filler-Embedded LDPE Zipper Bag
sources.authors: Y. Jo, E. Kim, S. Kim, C. Ban, S. Lim
sources.version_or_release: Foods 11(12), 1704 (published 2022-06-10); DOI 10.3390/foods11121704; CC BY open article
sources.locator: Full-text PDF: citation/publication lines 0–10; bag materials/making lines 89–121; film vapor test/storage conditions lines 134–159; moisture/activity/texture methods lines 167–187; retrieved 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read full published article PDF through a full-text mirror; original article URL and DOI verified from PDF citation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Filler-embedded LDPE film was 40–45 micrometers; zipper bags were 25 x 30.5 cm and made with a continuous band heat sealer. Water-vapor flux was measured after 24 h at 25 C/50% RH using a 135 mL double-deionized-water cup. Snacks were stored at 25 C/50% RH for 1, 5, 10, 15, or 20 days; food type influenced outcomes. Comparator typical and active zipper closures differ from sealed sample bags.
sources.applicability: Useful for actual package construction, fixed-condition comparison, and parallel mass/moisture/aw/texture observations. Does not establish performance for the cooperative's unknown product, bag type, or storage distribution.

sources.title: BRICE project: Understanding checking and breakage of biscuits and dry cereal products
sources.authors: P. Le-Bail, M. Bedas, B. Jaillais, C. Jonchère, L. Ribourg, A.M. Le Bail
sources.version_or_release: Conference/proceedings paper in Cereal Foods World 64(6) (2019); no software-style commit applies
sources.locator: PDF page 110, printed page A110, BRICE project abstract; opened 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z and targeted text retrieved 2026-10-10T06:28:03Z.
sources.observed_operation: Opened proceedings PDF and read project abstract; targeted publisher search result confirmed text.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Four-year project began in 2015. Study abstract compared round/thick biscuit with rectangular/thinner pierced biscuit; counted checking/breakage over 15 days; used Karl Fischer and automated NIR imaging for center/surface water; reports higher checking in the round/thick type and appearance within 1–2 days after baking. Detailed cooling line conditions are not disclosed in this short report.
sources.applicability: Supports the relevance of product geometry, moisture distribution, batch/shape tracking, and early observation points. It is an industry-collaborative comparator, not this snack or a film intervention.

sources.title: Understanding the factors affecting the seal integrity in heat sealed flexible food packages: A review
sources.authors: I. Ilhan, D. Turan, I. Gibson, R. ten Klooster
sources.version_or_release: Final published review, Packaging Technology and Science 34(6), 321–337 (2021); DOI 10.1002/pts.2564
sources.locator: TU Delft repository abstract, lines 77–84; opened 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Opened institutional repository record and read abstract plus linked-file availability; full PDF not opened.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Review groups heat-seal leak contributors as process parameters, material properties, contaminants, and further processes. It analyzes heat-seal mechanisms, form-fill-seal systems, and seal types. It is a review, not a failure diagnosis for this package.
sources.applicability: Supports considering both material and actual seal/process/contamination/handling history when a bag looks intact. No particular cause or setting may be inferred from the case anecdote.

sources.title: ASTM F1249-25, Standard Test Method for Water Vapor Transmission Rate Through Plastic Film and Sheeting Using a Modulated Infrared Sensor
sources.version_or_release: F1249-25, active version; last updated 2025-11-10; DOI 10.1520/F1249-25
sources.locator: ASTM standard summary, scope and significance/use sections; opened 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official ASTM standards catalog summary; normative document itself is not open access and was not downloaded.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Scope covers WVTR/permeance of flexible films and sheet up to 3 mm, single/multilayer polymers and foil, including coatings. Catalog states comparative use depends on agreed sampling, standardization, test conditions, and criteria; cautions simple scaling with thickness or vapor-pressure differential may not apply.
sources.applicability: Proposed method reference for comparing current and candidate film under defined common conditions. It does not test finished-package seals or establish product shelf life.

sources.title: ASTM F88/F88M-23, Standard Test Method for Seal Strength of Flexible Barrier Materials
sources.version_or_release: F88/F88M-23, active version displayed by ASTM; DOI 10.1520/F0088_F0088M-23
sources.locator: ASTM catalog scope and significance/use sections; publisher page opened 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z. Summary lines in initial catalog result identify process validation/control/capability and force/failure mode.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official ASTM catalog page for active version; normative document not downloaded.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Measures force needed to separate a sealed test strip and identifies failure mode; catalog states value is useful for process validation, control and capability, and recommends consistent use of one fixture/technique. Seal strength is not the same as package leak integrity.
sources.applicability: A proposed seal-process measurement, if the package is a compatible flexible barrier. Must be paired with an appropriate package-level leak check when leak status is the question.

sources.title: ASTM F2096-11(2019), Standard Test Method for Detecting Gross Leaks in Packaging by Internal Pressurization (Bubble Test)
sources.version_or_release: F2096-11(2019), active version displayed by ASTM; DOI 10.1520/F2096-11R19
sources.locator: ASTM catalog scope and significance/use sections; official page opened 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official ASTM catalog summary; normative document not downloaded.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Internal-pressurization bubble test for gross leaks; catalog states sensitivity down to 250 micrometers at 81% probability, is destructive because it requires package entry, and may be used for tray and pouch packages. Does not measure WVTR and cannot rule out smaller leaks.
sources.applicability: Possible proposed subset check only if format is suitable and method validated. It cannot demonstrate food safety, absence of every leak, or adequate moisture barrier.

sources.title: Influence of Packaging Material/Sealing on the Quality of Biscuits
sources.authors: R.M. Vercelino Alves, E.E.C. Garcia, M.R. Bordin
sources.version_or_release: Research article, Journal of Plastic Film & Sheeting 15(1), 57–71; first published 1999-01; DOI 10.1177/875608799901500107
sources.locator: SAGE version-of-record page, abstract and publication metadata, lines 20–41 and 143–151; opened 2026-10-10T06:34:11Z.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official SAGE journal page and read abstract, film descriptions, observed package comparison, and publication metadata; full article is restricted.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Study assessed six biscuit wrapper structures: BOPP/pearlized BOPP, BOPP/BOPP, BOPP/LDPE/BOPP, BOPP/met-BOPP, BOPP/LDPE/met-BOPP, PET/met-BOPP. Compared measured whole-package water-vapor transmission with theoretical values for 9 retail biscuit types from 6 manufacturers made on 3 form-fill-seal machine types. Material WVTRs were reported at 38 C/90% RH. Rollpack and horizontal flowpack packages had impaired transverse-seal integrity and measured WVT 1.1–3.0 times theoretical; vertical-flowpack package seals were reported as good. Full methods not accessible in the page preview.
sources.applicability: A directly relevant failed package/seal comparator showing the finished package and seal can depart from a flat-film calculation. Machine outcomes are specific to the study and do not identify a fix or setting for the cooperative; no maintenance-cost evidence was reported.

sources.title: Interactions between water and EVOH food packaging films
sources.authors: S. Aucejo, R. Catalá, R. Gavara
sources.version_or_release: Research article, Food Science and Technology International 6(2), 159–164 (2000); DOI 10.1177/108201320000600211; first published 2000-04
sources.locator: SAGE version-of-record page, abstract lines 23–32 and publication metadata lines 197–209; opened 2026-10-10T06:35:18Z. Full article restricted.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official SAGE journal page and read the abstract and bibliographic metadata; full article not accessed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Four EVOH copolymers were tested by continuous-flow permeation and gravimetric experiments at different RH and 23 ± 2 C. Water permeability was approximately constant over aw 0.3–0.75, then increased by up to two orders of magnitude above aw 0.75; ethylene content changed uptake/permeability.
sources.applicability: A condition-specific material-layer caveat only if a proposed/current film actually contains EVOH; it demonstrates why a barrier value without RH/temperature and layer details can mislead. Does not establish the cooperative film structure or its water-vapor result.

sources.title: Modeling Product Cooling for Baked and Snack Crackers
sources.version_or_release: Western Michigan University Honors Thesis, defended 2016-04-19; thesis record 2700
sources.locator: Western Michigan University repository record, abstract and access notice, lines 15–18 and 41–54; opened 2026-10-10T06:39:33Z.

critique_dispositions.response: Further source review and a complete revision were performed within the remaining whole-run window; stage records and final status avoid claiming that the investigator alone consumed the 60-minute window.

Define the package-level leak endpoint, batch/arm/timepoint reporting, method validation, detection limits, a fit-for-purpose integrity criterion, pre-unblind baseline and simulated-leak controls, and an owner-approved noninferiority margin. F2338-24 is a directly scoped candidate for flexible nonporous packages, subject to actual-format validation. A candidate must meet the owner-approved integrity criterion and be noninferior; comparison to a failing current baseline alone is insufficient. No unsupported numerical threshold is invented.

Three batches remain an illustrative exploratory plan only, not a minimum/power guarantee. Determine counts from baseline variability, meaningful effect, and capacity; no sample-size calculation performed.
Replace failed implementation language with impaired-seal comparison. Publisher abstract does not show an in-use failure or cooperative diagnosis.

Primary institutional abstract rechecked and supports the reported Crackerbread interval; full article retrieval timed out. Interval remains a non-transferable comparator and is excluded from decision rules.
Unknown product, package, process, distribution, endpoint, and lab inputs remain open; final proposal states what they prevent and what a modest pilot can learn.

validation_status.executed: Source searches and source-page/institutional-record reading, including listed primary-source reviser checks.
